utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Absolutely understood, Your Honour, but once again, the mere fact that one is qualified to testify as an expert doesn't necessarily mean that one is qualified to testify about all things that he is presented with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fair enough. All I'm saying -- okay, finish your comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I am in total agreement with you with regard to the general proposition. I am in absolute agreement with you. An expert obtains a different position with regard to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Because he’s not being tested on his recollection of events; he's coming to give an opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We're in agreement here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. But then in that event are you saying that an objection that a question is leading would be valid?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It would be valid depending on how one views him as an expert. He's an expert of what? He's proffered as an expert of history, he's proffered as an expert of political science, he's proffered as an expert of an interpretation of what somebody else believes is appropriate to do politically? I mean, they are different -- distinct issues. And to the extent that he's being proffered as a historical expert, I would stand in a position where I would not have any arguments with you whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand your argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might. Upon consideration and an understanding -- understanding what the Court has just said, at this point for purposes of this specific question, independent of the issue of mischaracterisation and -- I'll withdraw the objection, although I do have concerns about what the nature is of Mr. Treanor's expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, let's not conflate different topics in one --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm not trying to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's not do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm not trying to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You didn't rise objecting to the qualification of Mr. Treanor. You rose on that he is leading -- he is being led, rather, and that the Prosecutor is mischaracterising.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Correct, and within the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I'm dealing now with the objection that he is being led.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I'm saying, isn't it so that as an expert, it doesn't matter if he is an expert on politics, history, or what, but he sits here as an expert and therefore is entitled to read facts, recollect them, and then tender an opinion. And facts can be put to him. He doesn't have to remember those facts. They just have to be put to him, or he can read them from his report. And if I may just finish my question to you about that issue, I'm trying to look for that question again because it didn't look to me like it was leading in its nature. The question was: "Mr. Treanor, do you know of any other example where the FRY leadership were aware or made reference to the strategic objectives of the Bosnian Serbs?" That was the question. How does it lead? That's at page 96, line number --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm with you now. And the strict evidentiary response to that would be that you are correct if he's viewed as an expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Supposing he was not, how is it leading? The answer to that question is, Yes, I know, or, no, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So is it leading?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's not, and I've made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Then that objection is either overruled -- is overruled, unless you are withdrawing it. Madam, there is an objection that you are mischaracterising the evidence, calling things strategic objectives when they are called strategic goals. Do you have any response?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't see the distinction. Strategic goal is a strategic objective. An objective is a goal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I share what you say, but I do not sit here as an expert in English. May I suggest that we stick to the letter of the documents that we've been tendering, because it makes it very difficult for me to rule. I also don't know the difference between the two. I must go and consult my dictionary.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I will, too, Your Honour. If I haven't already, can we have Rule 65 ter number 06669.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could direct your attention to page 127 of the English and page 137 of the B/C/S. First of all, Mr. Treanor, what is this document?
This document is shorthand notes of the 1st session of the Council for Coordination of Points of View on State Policy, held on 11 August 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And who was in attendance at that meeting?
This meeting was attended by the --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The types of people --

-- the top leaders of the FRY; namely, Dobrica Cosic, who is the president; Milan Panic, who was the new prime minister; Slobodan Milosevic, who we referred to; Momir Bulatovic, we've also referred to; Vladislav Jovanovic, who was the foreign minister; Pavle Bulatovic, who was the minister of internal affairs of the FRY; General Zivota Panic, the Chief of Staff; and Milo Djukanovic, the president of the government or the prime minister of the Republic of Montenegro; and Radoman Bozovic, who was the president or prime minister of the government of the Government of the Republic of Serbia, who were described as members of this council. And there were other people there as well who were not members.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what discussion was had at this meeting about the strategic goals?

There's a brief discussion of the strategic goals on page 127 in the English. It's just a very short passage, so I can read it. Zivota Panic is speaking. He's describing the issue of the use of force in the territory of Yugoslavia, and his point 9 in his presentation is: "9. The possibility to control the Serbian side in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the wrong choice of strategic aims on the part of the Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina; namely, the takeover of Sarajevo. They constantly insist on taking over Sarajevo." Slobodan Milosevic then says: "Haven't they given it up?" And Zivota Panic replies: "Mr. President, they have not given it up. They had not given it up when we last spoke here with Prime Minister Panic. They were not so categorical, but they commented all the time that Sarajevo had to be taken over." Now, I must remark that the phrase "strategic aims" is the same phrase that has been translated in previous documents as "strategic goals."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may that document be -- the pages that we have referred to, be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: A quick point of clarification. I take it that document was obtained in the same fashion as the previous document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I would have to check on that, but I presume so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That was a document that was forwarded to you by the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm saying I will check on that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- but it's my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me get clear, is it your understanding that it is also a transcript of an audiotape which audiotape you are not in possession of?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I don't think that's the query, Your Honour. It's simply the source of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Explain yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. Is it a transcript of an audiotape, and is it a document -- and, in addition, is it a document that you received from the Serbian government?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you don't have an audio --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And you don't have the audio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You will check that, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I can, Your Honour, at the bottom of the second page in the English, it states who took the shorthand notes. As I stated at the beginning of my testimony about this document, these are shorthand notes of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We understand that they are shorthand notes. That is not the problem that we are faced with at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there would be no recording.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's an assumption that I'm not comfortable with at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I've been in meetings where there are people taking shorthand, and it's also been recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam, you will find out.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. So --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can that document, the pages that I took Mr. Treanor to, can they be admitted into evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. The pages of 06669 that were referred to are admitted into evidence. May they please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Those pages would be Exhibit P194, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And I note the time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Sutherland. Mr. Treanor, we are not done with you. You are supposed to come back at Monday, the 10th, at 9.00 in the morning, in this same court. Once again you are warned about not having to communicate with anybody about this case until you are excused from coming -- as a witness. Thank you very much. Court adjourned to Monday, the 10th, Courtroom II, at 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 10th day of November, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.03 p.m.,
